overview.title: Morocco’s Mediterranean national park
overview.p1: Al Hoceima National Park protects a rare and pristine stretch of Morocco's Mediterranean coastline: towering limestone cliffs, scrub-covered hills, and a rich marine reserve vital for seabirds and marine life.
overview.p2: Many of the park's finest hidden coves are accessible only by boat or longer coastal treks. Cala Iris and Torres de Alcalá sit on the park’s accessible western edge, serving as convenient gateways.
overview.p3: Be sure to pack plenty of water, high SPF sunscreen, and hire a local skipper or guide if you want to reach secluded beaches beyond roadside viewpoints.

q1.question: Do I need a local guide to visit?
q1.answer: Not for roadside lookouts or main village gateways, but hiring a guide or local boat skipper makes exploring remote coves and longer trails much safer and easier.

q2.question: Can I go swimming in the park?
q2.answer: Yes, swimming is possible in sheltered coves on calm days — always exercise caution in open sea waters.

q3.question: What is the best season to visit?
q3.answer: Spring and autumn are ideal for trekking and outdoor activities; summer is prime for boat excursions and swimming.

q4.question: How far is the park from Al Hoceima town?
q4.answer: The park boundaries start just west of town, with main access points like Cala Iris located roughly 50 km (about a 1-hour drive) away.

q5.question: What wildlife can I expect to see?
q5.answer: Ospreys and sea birds are key highlights; marine life including dolphins can occasionally be spotted offshore.
